title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this page and the previous one). Grothendieck is axiomatising a combinatorial 'analysis situs' through 'ateliers'. An atelier is a family F of 'figures' (subobjects) carrying two relations: ≤ (containment) and ≪ (a stronger, 'interior' containment). It has a subset L of 'lieux' (point-like figures) and a 'multistratification' M of strata. X ◁ F means that X is a stratum of the closure F̄ of the figure F. omb(X), the shadow of X, is the set of lieux x ≤ X.

Axiom At 8 (previous page). For a stratum X, put ∂X = Sup of the strata Y ◁ X with Y ≠ X. Then some lieu x satisfies x ≤ X but not x ≤ ∂X. Equivalently, the open shadow omb(X)° = omb(X) \ ∪_{Y◁X, Y≠X} omb(Y) is non-empty (1.52). The multishadow of a figure F is the set of omb(X) for X ◁ F with omb(X)° ≠ ∅; by At 8 this is all of F̄.

This page.
(1) It completes the Corollary begun on the previous page. For X, Y ∈ F̄ the following are equivalent:
- a) X ≤ Y (⇔ X ≪ Y);
- b) omb(X) ⊂ omb(Y);
- c) omb(X)° ⊂ omb(Y);
- d) omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅.
The implication d)⇒a) is the abstract analogue of the frontier condition of stratified spaces: if the open part of a stratum meets the closure of another, it lies in that closure. So the poset of strata is faithfully recorded by the set-theoretic shadows.
(2) Formula (1.53) gives a bijection F' ↦ multiomb(F') from Ssfig(F) = F_{≤F} (the subfigures of F) onto the subfigures of multiomb(F). Thus the abstract figure is determined by a concrete 'set-with-strata' model.
(3) A second Corollary follows: F has a certain property relative to a multistratification (the adjective is illegible) iff multiomb(F) has it.
(4) Remark on sub-ateliers. At 8 need not pass to a sub-atelier F', which in general is 'spécieux'. Call F' full ('plein') if F ∈ F', G ∈ F, G ≪ F imply G ∈ F'. In general L ∩ F' ⊂ L' (the lieux of F'), with equality for full sub-ateliers. A marginal note says it suffices that F' be L-full: F ∈ F', x ∈ L, x ≪ F ⇒ x ∈ F'. In that case At 8 for F implies At 8 for F', and omb(F) and multiomb(F) are the same whether computed in F or in F'.

Purpose. This is a step toward a 'tame topology' foundation (cf. Esquisse d'un programme §5): showing that abstract stratified ateliers can be realised by, and compared with, set-theoretic multistratifications. It also prepares the notion of (quasi-)embeddings of ateliers on the next page.
errors: The implication d)⇒a) is not justified on the page. It needs, besides At 8, that a lieu lies in the open part of exactly one stratum and that lieux are 'irreducible' (x ≤ Sup of strata ⇒ x ≤ one of them). Presumably these follow from earlier axioms not visible here.
The fullness condition is miswritten in the transcription as 'G ≪ F impliquent G ≪ F'; the image reads 'impliquent G ∈ F''.
The adjective in the second Corollary is illegible, so its exact content cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Axiom that every stratum has a non-empty open part, i.e. points not in its frontier
ideas.modern_name: non-emptiness of open strata / frontier axiom for abstract stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratified spaces); abstract poset versions in combinatorial topology

ideas.what: Equivalence of X ≤ Y with containment or intersection conditions on shadows
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition; recovery of the face/strata poset from closures
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Mather) and in regular CW / face-poset theory

ideas.what: Bijection between subfigures of F and subfigures of its multishadow (a set-theoretic model)
ideas.modern_name: representation of an abstract stratified lattice by a stratified set (Stone/Alexandrov-type realisation)

ideas.what: Full and L-full sub-ateliers inherit the axiom, and shadows are unchanged

missed.claim: An axiomatic, point-free theory of stratified 'ateliers' meant to found tame topology. It includes a representation theorem embedding an abstract atelier into a set-theoretic multistratification via shadows. It was never developed in the literature (o-minimality took a different, model-theoretic route).
missed.quote: Il y a une correspondance biunivoque F' ↦ multiomb(F'), Ssfig(F) ≃ Ssfig(multiomb(F))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could inform lattice-theoretic or point-free approaches to stratified spaces and exit-path or poset-stratified homotopy theory. Its interest is mainly historical, as a record of Grothendieck's own route toward tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are elementary order-theoretic facts about an abstract stratification framework. The framework itself (ateliers, ombres, multiombres) is an unpublished Grothendieck construction of historical interest, but this page contains no deep new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is 46, not 95.
'impliquent G ≪ F' should be 'impliquent G ∈ F''.
'en prenant celui-ci spécieux' is more likely 'en général celui-ci est spécieux'.
Marginal note reads: 'il suffit qu'il soit L-plein, i.e. que F ∈ F', x ∈ L, x ≪ F ⇒ x ∈ F''.
In the second Corollary, 'dimension[?]' is uncertain; the word is illegible.
